Keywords: ga4 config tag gtm setup base tag measurement id G-XXXXXXXX
Description: The foundational GA4 tag that must fire on every page. Sets up the GA4 connection and enables base tracking (page views, sessions).
Implementation: Tag Type: Google Analytics: GA4 Configuration. Enter Measurement ID (G-XXXXXXXX from GA4 Data Stream). Fire on All Pages trigger. Publish immediately.
Do: Create a GTM variable for the Measurement ID so you can update it in one place. Add 'Send to server-side container' if using server-side GTM.
Dont: Don't hardcode the Measurement ID in each tag (use a variable). Don't fire on page preview/edit URLs in CMS. Don't duplicate this tag.

Keywords: ga4 event custom event form submit button click purchase conversion tracking
Description: Fires a specific GA4 event with custom parameters when a user action occurs (form submit, button click, add to cart, etc.)
Implementation: Tag Type: Google Analytics: GA4 Event. Connect to Configuration Tag. Set Event Name (snake_case). Add Event Parameters (optional: form_type, button_text, item_id). Fire on specific trigger.
Trigger: Custom triggers: form submission, button click, timer, custom event from dataLayer
Do: Name events consistently (snake_case). Include the GA4 Configuration tag connection. Use GTM's built-in variables (Page URL, Click Text) as parameter values.
Dont: Don't use spaces or uppercase in event names. Don't forget to test in Preview Mode before publishing. Don't create duplicate events with similar names.

Keywords: google ads conversion tag tracking purchase lead adwords gtag AW-XXXXXXXXX
Description: Fires when a conversion occurs (purchase, lead form submit) to feed data back to Google Ads for Smart Bidding optimization.
Implementation: Tag Type: Google Ads Conversion Tracking. Enter Conversion ID (AW-XXXXXXXXXX) and Conversion Label (from Google Ads). Set conversion value dynamically via dataLayer variable (for purchase). Fire on conversion event trigger.
Trigger: Trigger: Custom Event matching purchase or lead confirmation page
Do: Always include conversion value for revenue-based bidding (ROAS). Use dataLayer to pass dynamic values. Link GA4 as your conversion source for accuracy (import from GA4 in Google Ads).
Dont: Don't hardcode conversion values (use dynamic dataLayer values). Don't fire on every page (only on confirmation/thank you page). Don't use this AND GA4 import simultaneously — choose one source.

Keywords: facebook pixel meta pixel event code conversion tracking fbq function
Description: Fires the Facebook/Meta Pixel to track website actions for ad optimization, custom audiences, and conversion reporting.
Implementation: Tag Type: Custom HTML. Paste Meta Pixel base code + fbq('track', 'Purchase', {value: X, currency: 'USD'}) for events. OR use Meta Pixel GTM template from Tag Manager gallery.
Trigger: All Pages (base code) + Custom Event trigger (for specific events like Purchase, Lead, AddToCart)
Do: Use Meta Pixel Helper Chrome extension to verify. Use Conversions API (CAPI) alongside pixel for iOS privacy. Include event deduplication (eventID) for CAPI + pixel combo.
Dont: Don't use only Pixel without CAPI (iOS14+ broke browser-only tracking). Don't forget to test in Meta Events Manager. Don't track identical events twice without deduplication.

Keywords: google tag gtag gtm base new google tag multi-destination unified
Description: The new unified 'Google Tag' (as of 2023) replaces the gtag.js snippet and Google Ads global site tag. Sends data to multiple Google destinations from one tag.
Implementation: Tag Type: Google Tag. Enter your Google Tag ID (same as GA4 Measurement ID, or Google Ads account ID). Link destinations (GA4, Google Ads, Merchant Center) in the Google tag configuration.
Do: If migrating from old setup, remove existing GA4 Config tag and Google Ads Global Site Tag — replace with single Google Tag. Use the tag's Configuration section to manage all destinations.
Dont: Don't have both a Google Tag AND a GA4 Configuration tag for the same property (creates duplicate data). Don't skip verifying in GA4 DebugView after publishing.

Keywords: datalayer push event variable data pass gtm javascript custom data
Description: The dataLayer is GTM's communication bridge — JavaScript pushes data to dataLayer, GTM reads it and uses it in tags. Critical for passing dynamic values (order total, user ID, product name).
Implementation: In site code: dataLayer.push({event: 'purchase', transaction_id: '12345', value: 99.99, currency: 'USD'}). In GTM: create Data Layer Variable for each key you push. Use in tags as variable references.
Trigger: Custom Event trigger that fires when the dataLayer event name matches
Do: Work with dev to define a dataLayer spec before implementation. Push the event AFTER data is available (not before transaction_id is populated). Test in GTM Preview → Variables.
Dont: Don't rely on CSS selectors for revenue values (they change with design updates). Don't push events before data is ready. Don't forget to document your dataLayer spec.

Keywords: scroll depth tracking trigger percentage page engagement content consumption
Description: Tracks how far users scroll down a page (25%, 50%, 75%, 90%, 100%). Useful for understanding content engagement.
Implementation: GTM: Trigger → Scroll Depth. Set vertical scroll thresholds (25, 50, 75, 90). Enable for all pages or specific pages. Create GA4 Event tag firing on this trigger with event name 'scroll_depth' and parameter 'scroll_depth_percentage'.
Do: Use to identify where users stop reading on long-form pages. Compare scroll depth by device type. Correlate with conversion rates to understand if content length is appropriate.
Dont: Don't create a separate event for every 5% interval (too granular). Don't use scroll tracking as the only engagement metric. Don't forget to include the page URL parameter.

Keywords: consent mode v2 gdpr cookie consent cookieless tracking signal google ads
Description: Google Consent Mode v2 lets you use cookieless pings when users decline tracking. Required for Google Ads in EEA from March 2024. Enables Google to model conversion data even without cookies.
Implementation: Integrate with your CMP (Cookiebot, OneTrust, Usercentrics). Use their GTM template. Set default state to 'denied'. Update consent on user choice. GA4 and Google Ads automatically respect consent signals.
Do: Implement Consent Mode v2 if you have EU traffic (legally required). Work with your CMP vendor's official GTM template. Test with Google Tag Diagnostics.
Dont: Don't implement without a proper CMP (using fake 'denied' states to bypass is against policy). Don't skip testing — incorrect implementation means lost conversion data. Don't ignore the March 2024 enforcement deadline.

Keywords: click tracking button link custom click event element specific class id
Description: Track specific button clicks, link clicks, or element interactions that aren't captured by Enhanced Measurement.
Implementation: GTM: Enable built-in Click variables (Click ID, Click Classes, Click Text, Click URL). Create a Click trigger. Filter by Click Classes or Click ID to target specific buttons. Fire GA4 Event tag.
Trigger: Click Trigger: All Clicks or Just Links, filtered by CSS selector (Click Classes contains 'cta-button')
Do: Use Click Text variable to capture what was clicked (great for CTA testing). Use GTM Preview to verify the right elements are triggering. Combine with GA4 to see which CTAs convert.
Dont: Don't use 'All Clicks' trigger without filtering (fires on every element). Don't use fragile selectors that change with design updates. Don't forget to test on mobile (click vs tap).
